introduction.text: Casa di Diana is a Roman insula in Regio I of Ostia, notable for its multi‑storey residential layout, surviving mosaics, frescoes, and a terracotta relief of the goddess Diana that gives the complex its name.

history.description: Construction of the insula in the mid‑2nd century AD, likely on the site of an earlier domus.
Dating of the mitre to the late 2nd or early 3rd century AD.
Discovery of the mitre during excavations in 1914‑1915.
Excavations by Guido Calza between 1914 and 1916.
Excavations by Alfredo Marinucci between 1994 and 1997.

design.description: The insula is organised around a central porticoed courtyard, with multiple floors, arcades, a cistern, and a terracotta relief of Diana above the cistern.

art.description: Frescoed rooms, mosaics on the ground floor, and a terracotta relief of Diana depicting her with a bow, arrow, dog, and deer.
